LESSON: SINGING GAMES- AFRICAN STYLE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Appreciation
Topic 3.1: Singing Games- African Style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Singing Games- African Style, part of Appreciation in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we make singing game in African Style interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify roles of the performers in the African style singing game,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Singing Games- African Style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify costumes used in the performance of a singing game in African style,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Singing Games- African Style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify props used in a singing game in African style,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Singing Games- African Style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. imitate activities involved in a singing game in African style ,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Singing Games- African Style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. identify formations used in African style singing games,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Singing Games- African Style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate performances of African style singing games for cultural awareness. • Learners to watch recorded or live performances of singing games in African style, and identify songs in the performance. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Singing Games- African Style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: as the learner imitates and performs various activities involved in singing games in African

style.

● Communication and collaboration: as the learner speaks clearly while discussing roles of performers in the singing game

in African style,

● Digital literacy: as the learner searches and watches recorded performances of singing games in African style using digital

devices.

● Citizenship: as the learner expresses pride while performing African singing games from diverse Kenyan communities.

Values:
● Respect: is enhanced as the learner appreciates diverse opinions while discussing how costumes are used while performing

singing games in African style.

● Unity: is promoted as the learner displays team spirit as they talk about various roles of performers in the singing games in

African style, watched.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: is nurtured as the learner displays team spirit as they work in pairs to discuss various pattern formations

involved in the singing game in African style.

43

Link to other learning areas:

Environmental Activities: as learner applies knowledge and skills learnt in Environmental activities to search for singing

games in African style.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Flash cards, digital devices, musical instruments, pictures, reference books, audio /visual recordings of african style singing

games, relevant virtual sites, relevant props and costumes, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces,

weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input

devices such as head wand
